Unremarkable

/un-rih-MAR-kuh-bul/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Unremarkable means not notable or interesting; ordinary to the point of attracting no attention.

Unremarkable means not notable or interesting; ordinary to the point of attracting no attention. The famous physicist grew up in an unremarkable farming town so small that most road maps did not even label it.

Worked Example

For three quarters, the scout found the visiting point guard thoroughly unremarkable, just another steady player doing nothing that stood out from the crowd. Then, in the final five minutes, she scored fifteen straight points and changed his report entirely.

For most of the game, nothing about the player's performance drew any attention at all, which is what made it unremarkable until the finish.

How Unremarkable Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

ordinary

ordinary: normal, with nothing special about it

nondescript

nondescript: lacking distinctive features

forgettable

forgettable: easily slipping out of memory

Antonyms

extraordinary

extraordinary: far beyond what is usual

striking

striking: attracting attention immediately

How Strong Is It? — plain → unremarkable → featureless

plain vs. unremarkable

plain vs. unremarkable: Something plain is simple and undecorated, while something unremarkable is so ordinary that nobody gives it a second glance.

featureless vs. unremarkable

featureless vs. unremarkable: An unremarkable place blends into the background, but a featureless one has nothing distinctive about it that you could describe at all.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of unremarkable.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — un-

Prefix — un-: not

Root — remark

Root — remark: from French remarquer, to mark out, to notice

Suffix — -able

Suffix — -able: able to be, worthy of

Put it together

Put it together: Unremarkable stacks un-, 'not,' onto remark, from French remarquer, 'to mark out or notice,' plus -able, 'worthy of.' Something remarkable is literally 'worth marking,' worth pointing out, so something unremarkable is not worth pointing out at all.

Use the root in a new word: earmark

Use the root in a new word: earmark: Lawmakers voted to earmark the surplus funds for bridge repairs, literally 'marking' the money for one purpose, using the same root of marking and noticing that hides inside unremarkable.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Unremarkable is usually mildly negative in everyday speech, but in medical reports it is good news: 'the scan was unremarkable' means the doctors found nothing unusual or worrying. Context decides whether being unnoticeable is a flaw or a relief.
